title: A scalar-fraction criterion for a localization functor
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $\mathcal C$ an $R$-linear triangulated category with $R$-linear integer shifts [def-weil-linear-category], [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Let $M\subseteq R$ be a submonoid, let $Q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C[M^{-1}]$ be [sk-def-sfb-rationalization], and let $\mathcal D$ be a preadditive $R$-linear category. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be an additive $R$-linear functor [def-weil-linear-functor]. Suppose that $F$ is essentially surjective, inverts $W_M$, and $m\operatorname{id}_Y$ is invertible for every $m\in M$ and $Y\in\mathcal D$. Assume, for all $A,B\in\mathcal C$: (i) for every $h:FA\to FB$ there are $m\in M$ and $u:A\to B$ with $mh=F(u)$; (ii) if $F(u)=F(v)$ then $nu=nv$ for some $n\in M$. Then the induced functor $G:\mathcal C[M^{-1}]\to\mathcal D$ is fully faithful and essentially surjective, and $F$ is a localization at $W_M$ in the universal-property sense of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. No triangulated structure on $\mathcal D$ is required.

source.place: Morphisms of the rationalization, full faithfulness, and conclusion; generic algebraic assembly extracted by the agent

proof.text: Put $\mathcal L=\mathcal C[M^{-1}]$. By [sk-def-sfb-rationalization], $Q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal L$ is a triangulated localization at $W_M$; in particular it is additive by [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Apply [lem-sfb-additive-localization-linear] to this additive localization. Thus $Q(rf)=rQ(f)$, and every $X\in\mathcal L$ admits $A\in\mathcal C$ and an isomorphism $QA\cong X$. We use this canonical $R$-linear structure on $\mathcal L$. Also every $m\in M$ acts invertibly on $\mathcal L$ by [sk-def-sfb-rationalization].

source.place: Morphisms of the rationalization: localization, its linear structure and scalar invertibility

proof.text: Since $F$ inverts $W_M$, clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] gives $G:\mathcal L\to\mathcal D$ and a natural isomorphism $\eta:G\circ Q\xrightarrow{\sim}F$. The hypotheses of [lem-sfb-linear-localization-descent] apply: $Q$ is an additive $R$-linear localization by step 1, both target categories are preadditive and $R$-linear, and $F$ is additive and $R$-linear. Hence $G(r\alpha)=rG(\alpha)$. This assertion needs no shift or triangles on $\mathcal D$.

source.place: Full faithfulness: factor the functor through the rationalization

proof.text: For $A,B\in\mathcal C$ and $\alpha:QA\to QB$, write $T_{A,B}(\alpha)=\eta_B\circ G(\alpha)\circ\eta_A^{-1}:FA\to FB$. Conjugation by these isomorphisms is a bijection of Hom sets. Naturality of $\eta$ gives $T_{A,B}(Q(u))=F(u)$, and $R$-bilinearity of composition [def-weil-linear-category], together with step 2, gives $T_{A,B}(r\alpha)=rT_{A,B}(\alpha)$. These formulas keep track of the comparison isomorphisms rather than identifying $GQA$ with $FA$.

source.place: Full faithfulness: identify the comparison map on Hom sets

proof.text: To prove surjectivity of $T_{A,B}$, take $h:FA\to FB$. Hypothesis (i) supplies $m\in M$ and $u:A\to B$ with $mh=F(u)$. Let $s=m\operatorname{id}_{QB}$ and put $\alpha=s^{-1}\circ Q(u)$, using scalar invertibility from [sk-def-sfb-rationalization]. Bilinearity gives $m\alpha=s\circ\alpha=Q(u)$. Step 3 therefore gives $mT_{A,B}(\alpha)=F(u)=mh$. Since $m\operatorname{id}_{FB}$ is invertible by hypothesis, composing this equality on the left with its inverse gives $T_{A,B}(\alpha)=h$. Thus $G$ is full on the objects in the image of $Q$.

source.place: Full faithfulness: denominator lifting gives surjectivity on localized Hom sets

proof.text: Suppose $T_{A,B}(\alpha)=T_{A,B}(\beta)$. Clause 1 of [lem-sfb-rationalization-scalar-fractions] supplies $m,n\in M$ and $u,v:A\to B$ with $m\alpha=Q(u)$ and $n\beta=Q(v)$. Since $Q$ preserves scalars by step 1 and $R$ is commutative, $Q(nu)=mn\alpha$ and $Q(mv)=mn\beta$. Applying the formulas of step 3 gives $F(nu)=mnT_{A,B}(\alpha)=mnT_{A,B}(\beta)=F(mv)$. Hypothesis (ii), applied to the two integral arrows $nu,mv:A\to B$, now gives $p\in M$ with $pnu=pmv$.

source.place: Full faithfulness: common denominators reduce equality to integral arrows

proof.text: Apply $Q$ to $pnu=pmv$ and use $Q(rf)=rQ(f)$ from step 1. The two fraction equations of step 5 give $pmn\alpha=pmn\beta$. The product $pmn$ belongs to $M$, so $pmn\operatorname{id}_{QB}$ is invertible by [sk-def-sfb-rationalization]. Since $pmn\alpha=(pmn\operatorname{id}_{QB})\circ\alpha$ and likewise for $\beta$, compose with the inverse to obtain $\alpha=\beta$. This proves injectivity of $T_{A,B}$ and hence faithfulness of $G$ on objects in the image of $Q$.

source.place: Full faithfulness: cancel the product of all three denominators

proof.text: For arbitrary $X,Y\in\mathcal L$, choose $e:QA\xrightarrow{\sim}X$ and $d:QB\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ from step 1. The bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(X,Y)\to\operatorname{Hom}(QA,QB)$ sends $a$ to $d^{-1}\circ a\circ e$, and its inverse sends $b$ to $d\circ b\circ e^{-1}$. On target Hom sets use the same formulas with $G(e),G(d)$. Functoriality of $G$ makes this square commute, so the bijectivity already proved on $QA,QB$ proves that $G$ is fully faithful everywhere. For $Z\in\mathcal D$, essential surjectivity of $F$ gives $A$ and $FA\cong Z$; composing with $\eta_A:GQA\cong FA$ gives $GQA\cong Z$. Thus $G$ is essentially surjective.

source.place: Full faithfulness and essential surjectivity: extend from image objects by explicit conjugation

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fully-faithful-ess-surj-equivalence] to $G$, which is fully faithful and essentially surjective by step 7. Working throughout in a common sufficiently large universe, we obtain a quasi-inverse $H:\mathcal D\to\mathcal L$ and natural isomorphisms $H\circ G\cong\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal L}$ and $G\circ H\cong\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal D}$.

source.place: Conclusion: the induced functor is an equivalence

proof.text: For any category $\mathcal E$, precomposition with $G$ from $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal D,\mathcal E)$ to $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal L,\mathcal E)$ has quasi-inverse precomposition with $H$: applying a functor to the two natural isomorphisms of step 8 gives the two required natural isomorphisms on functor categories, also on transformations by naturality. Precomposition with $Q$ is an equivalence onto the full category $\operatorname{Fun}_{W_M}(\mathcal C,\mathcal E)$ of functors inverting $W_M$, by the localization property in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. The composite of these two equivalences is precomposition with $G\circ Q$: its inverse is the composite of their quasi-inverses in reverse order, and its unit and counit are obtained by composing theirs. Whiskering $\eta:G\circ Q\cong F$ by each functor to $\mathcal E$ identifies this composite naturally with precomposition with $F$. Consequently precomposition with $F$ is the required equivalence for every $\mathcal E$. Together with the assumed inversion of $W_M$, this proves exactly the asserted localization universal property.

source.place: Conclusion: transfer the full functor-category universal property through the equivalence

split_report.summary: Expanded the scalar-fraction localization criterion into a factorization, scalar compatibility, explicit denominator-lifting surjectivity, common-denominator faithfulness, passage to all objects, and transport of the functor-category universal property. Reused the existing fraction node, linear localization leaves, universal-property leaf and equivalence criterion. No new nodes and no statement change. No triangulated target is used.
